## Introduction

Returning to the fundamental question of installation type, some recent discussions have provided new perspectives on the distinction of piëzometers.
As an extra challenge, I will connect to the new data warehouse, and see what happens / how long I can stand it.


Piezometer refers to pressure measurement, whereas water level might also be measured by divers?
Yet, in contrast, at least some sources (among which my ~~favorite~~ [ex-favorite reference](https://www.h2o-watermatters.com/includes/partials/printArticle.php?ed=201904&art=06_Artikel)) distinguish the two installation types by filter length (hold this thought).
The well might be open ("filter") only at the tip, or over a longer stretch of the tube.
We distinguish

> groundwater observation well (fully perforated) and a deep piezometer (short perforated filter)


But this interpretation bears a paradox:
```{r, echo=FALSE, out.width = "100%", fig.cap = "<i>Distribution of filter lengths of all sites registered in the watina database.</i>"}
knitr::include_graphics("figures/filterlength_distribution.svg")
```

We only place filters of certain, distinct lengths (0.3 m, 0.5 m, or 1.0 m).


In a technical discussion about the database (02/10/2024, FM with Frederic Piesschaert and Jo Loos), it became apparent that the distinguishing feature might be the position of the filter top with respect to water table.
(This is consistent with the figure in the reference above, despite the misleading caption).

## Water Table
**Water table** is defined as the zero iso-pressure surface, i.e. the layer in the soil where capillary pressure (or, generally, attractive interactions of water-water-soil) exactly compensate the hydrostatic pressure ([see this illustrative video](https://www.elementaryengineeringlibrary.com/civil-engineering/soil-mechanics/capillary-rise-in-soils)).
Note that the hydrostatic case is a special case of ground water configuration in which there is negligible ground-water flow [Dingman 2014, p.350].

```{r, echo=FALSE, out.width = "100%", fig.cap = "<i>Definition of the water table.</i>"}
knitr::include_graphics("https://www.elementaryengineeringlibrary.com/images/chapters-images/0056-10-stress-in-water.png")
```

```{r}
locs %<>%

    mutate(tubelength = ifelse(PeilbuisLengte <= 0,

           loc_validity = MeetpuntStatus,
           loc_typecode = MeetpuntTypeCode,
           loc_typename = MeetpuntType,
           obswell_code = PeilpuntCode,
           obswell_rank = PeilpuntVersie,

obswells_db <- locs
```

# Water Level
As before, slightly modified:
```{r}
query_peilmeting <- function() {
  water_query <- tbl(watina_dwh, "FactPeilMeting") %>%
    select(PeilpuntWID, MeetpuntWID, 
      PeilmetingCategorieCode, PeilMetingTypeCode, 
      DatumWID, 
      Niveau, mTAW, mMaaiveld,
      PeilmetingStatus
      ) %>%
    arrange(DatumWID)
  
  tijd <- tbl(watina_dwh, "DimDatum") %>%
    select(DatumWID, HydroJaar)
  
  water_query %<>%
    left_join(tijd, join_by(DatumWID)) %>%
    rename(
      id = PeilpuntWID,
      loc_id = MeetpuntWID,
      hydroyear = HydroJaar
      )
  return (water_query)
}

water_zwin <- query_peilmeting() %>%
  filter(loc_id == loc_selection) %>%
  collect() %>%
  mutate_at(vars(
    PeilMetingTypeCode,
    PeilmetingCategorieCode,
    PeilmetingStatus,
    hydroyear
  ), as.factor) %>%
  mutate(
    date = lubridate::ymd(DatumWID),
  )
glimpse(water_zwin)
```


```{r}
water_zwin %>%
  mutate_at(vars(id), as.factor) %>%

  geom_line(aes(x = date, y = mTAW), linetype = "dotted") +
```

**INSIGHT:** `Niveau` still seems to be the better water level than `mMaaiveld`...


Here is a function to get a level ratio for a given location.

```{r}
submerge_fraction <- 0.666
level_threshold <- function (water_levels, reference_levels) {
  # calculate what fraction of level measurements at a given location
  # is above a chosen reference (for use with e.g. filterdepth).

  ref_count <- water_levels %>% 
    filter(!is.na(Niveau)) %>% 
    inner_join(reference_levels, by = join_by(id)) %>%
    group_by(id) %>%
    summarize(
      above_reference = sum(Niveau > -reference) / n()
      ) %>%
    mutate(is_piezometer = as.factor(above_reference > submerge_fraction))
  return(ref_count)

}

ref_zwin <- zwin %>% 
  select(id, filtertop_depth) %>% 
  rename(reference = filtertop_depth) %>% 
  collect
# reference_levels <- ref %>% collect 
# water_levels <- water_zwin %>% collect

zwin_submerged <- level_threshold(water_zwin, ref_zwin)  

```

Try with the rest:
```{r}

water_levels <- query_peilmeting() %>%
  collect() %>%
  mutate_at(vars(
    PeilMetingTypeCode,
    PeilmetingCategorieCode,
    PeilmetingStatus,
    hydroyear
  ), as.factor) %>%
  mutate(
    date = lubridate::ymd(DatumWID),
  )

ref <- obswells_db %>% 
  select(id, filtertop_depth) %>% 
  rename(reference = filtertop_depth) %>% 
  collect


obswell_submerged <- obswells_db %>%
  collect %>%
  left_join(level_threshold(water_levels, ref), by = join_by(id))

```


```{r}
obswell_submerged %>% 
    rename(fraction_levels_above_filtertop = above_reference) %>% 
    ggplot(aes(x = fraction_levels_above_filtertop, fill = is_piezometer)) +
    geom_histogram(bins = 256) +
    scale_y_continuous(trans = "log10")
```

```{r}
obswell_submerged %>%
  filter(!is.na(is_piezometer)) %>% 
  group_by(obswell_type, is_piezometer) %>%
  tally() %>% 
  tidyr::spread(is_piezometer, n)

```


Just to check, repeat the filtertop depth distribution:

```{r}
obswell_submerged %>% 
  filter(between(filterdepth, 0, 5)) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = filtertop_depth, fill = is_piezometer)) +
    geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(count)),
      binwidth = 0.05,
      colour = "black"
    ) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = c(0, 0.3)) +
    scale_x_reverse() +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("#f0d70f", "#8eafd7", "#b2b2b2", "#284971")) +
    coord_flip() +
    xlab("filter top depth (m; positive: down)") +
    guides(fill = guide_legend(title = "well is piezometer?")) +
    theme(text = element_text(size = 20))

ggsave("figures/piezometers_by_submerged_filter.pdf",
    dpi = 300, width = 16, height = 8, units = "in"
  )
```

# DWH Translation
_notes for DWH migration_

- `vwDimMeetpunt` -> `DimMeetpunt`
- `vwDimGebied` -> `DimGebied`
- `Use of .data in tidyselect expressions was deprecated in tidyselect 1.2.0. Please use "colname" instead of "colname"` in get_locs()
- is `PeilpuntStatusCode` defined by `loc_validity`?
- `PeilpuntOpenbaarheidTypeCode` outsourced to `DimOpenbaarheid`
- include `filtertop_depth`?
- `DimTijd` -> `DimDatum`
- `TijdWID` -> `DatumWID`
